package_info.why_malicious: Vulnerable versions of Drupal Core allow authenticated users to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of another user's session via a reflected DOM XSS vulnerability in rejected forms. This enables attackers to hijack accounts, steal session data, and inject persistent malicious content.

execution_context.trigger: Submission of a form with an expired or invalid CSRF token (rejected form submission)
execution_context.file_location: node/add/[type] and node/[node-id]/edit endpoints (form handler, CKEditor integration)
required_permissions: permission to create or edit content with Full HTML mode enabled

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a form is submitted with an expired or invalid CSRF token, the server reflects the submitted content (including malicious HTML/JavaScript) unsanitized in the error page, CKEditor renders the reflected content, and the injected JavaScript executes in the user's browser context, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The snippet demonstrates that user-supplied HTML and JavaScript are reflected and executed in the browser without sanitization, enabling cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, user input in rejected or error states should be strictly sanitized and never allow script execution. Here, the input is reflected unsanitized, violating secure input handling practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve reflecting user content in error pages to help users recover their input after a failed submission, but never in a way that allows script execution or HTML injection.
key_indicators: User input reflected unsanitized in HTML context of error/rejection pages
Presence and execution of <script> tags in CKEditor-enabled fields
Bypass of CKEditor script filtering via <iframe> embedding
Error pages rendering user-supplied HTML/JS after form rejection

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts and submits a POST request to node/add/[type] or node/[node-id]/edit with malicious HTML/JavaScript in a CKEditor-enabled field (such as body[0][value]), using Full HTML mode.
attack_chain.leads_to: The form is rejected due to a missing or invalid CSRF token, but the malicious content is reflected unsanitized in the error page.

attack_chain.action: CKEditor on the error page renders the reflected content, including the injected <iframe> and <script> tags.
attack_chain.leads_to: The injected JavaScript executes in the victim's browser context, allowing arbitrary code execution.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript can hijack user sessions, steal credentials, or inject further malicious content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Account compromise, data theft, or further exploitation of the victim's session.

behavioral_signatures: Reflection of user-supplied HTML or JavaScript in error or rejected form pages
Execution of <script> tags in CKEditor fields after form rejection
Presence of <iframe> and <script> tags in form field values submitted to content creation or editing endpoints
file_indicators: node/add/* and node/*/edit endpoints where error messages reflect form field content
CKEditor-enabled fields (e.g., body[0][value]) containing suspicious HTML or JavaScript code
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests to node/add/* or node/*/edit endpoints with HTML/JavaScript payloads in form fields
Subsequent outbound requests or actions triggered by injected JavaScript, such as requests to credential exfiltration endpoints or unexpected third-party domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor POST requests to content creation and editing endpoints for HTML or JavaScript payloads in CKEditor-enabled fields, especially when followed by form rejection errors. Inspect error pages for unsanitized reflection of user input. Deploy web application firewalls (WAF) to block script tags in form fields, and audit CKEditor configuration to ensure script filtering is enforced. Regularly review error page templates for proper input sanitization.
